newsitem.title: DENMARK: Berendsen profits down, hopes up.
newsitem.headline: Berendsen profits down, hopes up.

text.p: Danish holding group Sophus Berendsen on Thursday posted considerably lower 1996 profits due to losses in its electronics and data division but said it was optimistic about the outlook for 1997.
Berendsen reported net profits of 910 million crowns ($139 million) for last year, down from the previous year's 960 million crowns, but in line with expectations.
Group pre-tax profits before earnings from part-owned British-based Rentokil Initial were 146 million crowns against 1995's 275 million crowns.

Berendsen said that Rentokil's acquisition of British business services firm BET for some 20 billion crowns was the most important event of 1996, a move which caused its Rentokil holding to fall from around 52 percent to 38.5 percent.

But it was problems with its electronics and data division, and to a lesser degree its power and motion control division, which dented Berendsen's 1996 group profits. The future of the two sections looked good, however, due to rationalisation programmes, the report said.
"1996 was a very difficult year for the electronics and data division, the results were exceeedingly unsatisfactory," Berendsen added.
The division showed an operating loss of 44.5 million crowns in 1996 from a 36.3 million profit the year before, mainly due to problems with data companies in Denmark and Sweden.
Berendsen said the division underwent major restructuring in autumn 1996, into separate international business units for electronics, electrical technology and data.
It said rationalisation schemes had been carried out, cost control and logistics strengthened, with the focus now on high quality niche, rather than low gross margin, products.
New directors had been appointed, it said, giving rise to expectations that the division would return to profit in 1997.

It said that its power and motion unit had a disappointing year, with operating profits halved to 76.3 million crowns from 1995's 148 million surplus but logistics improvements and cost cutting were expected to bring a much better result this year.

Berendsen's textile service did well in 1996, with operating profits 26 percent up at 205.4 million crowns on 19 percent bigger turnover, while there were good growth prospects for Rentokil Initial in 1997, it said.
"Against this background and on the basis of stable currency exchange rates and market conditions, we expect good progress in 1997," Berendsen said.
The 1996 result exactly mirrored analyst expectations of an average 146 million crown profit before tax and earnings from its associated company Rentokil Initial.
Berendsen issued a profits warning last November acknowledging problems with its electronics and data division.
The Berendsen share was little affected by the disappointing 1996 result, which was already discounted. It closed two crowns down at 825. --Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652 ($ = 6.561 Danish Crowns)
